entities.description: Yang (陽) is one of the two fundamental and complementary principles of Chinese cosmology, philosophy, and traditional medicine. Yang is the active, creative, light, warm, ascending, and expansive principle — the bright face of the mountain, the sun, the sky. It is not good or bad in itself; balance between yin and yang is the ideal. In the I Ching yang is represented by an unbroken line (⚊). The three yang trigrams are: Heaven (Qian ☰, pure yang), Thunder (Zhen ☳, eldest son), Water (Kan ☵, middle son), and Mountain (Gen ☶, youngest son). In Chinese medicine yang governs the exterior and the function of organs; yin governs the interior and substance. Yang corresponds broadly to: light, day, sun, summer, fire, heat, activity, the masculine, heaven, ascending, outward, and the initiating creative impulse. It is the complement and counterpart of Yin, never truly separate — the Taijitu (☯) symbol shows each containing a seed of the other.

Yin (陰) is one of the two fundamental and complementary principles of Chinese cosmology, philosophy, and traditional medicine. Yin is the receptive, dark, cool, descending, contracting, and sustaining principle — the shaded face of the mountain, the moon, the earth. It is not inferior to Yang; balance between the two is the ideal. In the I Ching yin is represented by a broken line (⚋). The four yin trigrams are: Earth (Kun ☷, pure yin), Wind (Xun ☴, eldest daughter), Fire (Li ☲, middle daughter), and Lake (Dui ☱, youngest daughter). In Chinese medicine yin governs the interior and substance of organs; yang governs function and exterior. Yin corresponds broadly to: darkness, night, moon, winter, water, cold, rest, the feminine, earth, descending, inward, and the receiving sustaining ground. It is the complement and counterpart of Yang — the Taijitu (☯) symbol shows each containing a seed of the other.
